title: fix(codex): Ultrafast drops to Fast after the first turn with ChatGPT sign-in
body:
Closes #169264

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex turns drop from Ultrafast to Fast after the first message in a conversation when signed in with ChatGPT.

## User Impact

User impact: people who select Ultrafast now get it on every turn their account supports, not only the first. Other providers and accounts without Ultrafast are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

For ChatGPT sign-in, OpenClaw stores conversations without a provider on purpose. On resumed and follow-up turns, the Ultrafast check read that empty provider as "not OpenAI" and skipped itself. The check now falls back to the run's own provider, the same fallback this file already uses for model-call reporting. The account's catalog still decides whether Ultrafast is sent.

Found and diagnosed with Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code): our live Codex logs showed only the first turn of each conversation on Ultrafast. We traced that to this check and confirmed that Codex itself treats a missing provider as `openai` (`codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs:3816-3819`, rust-v0.160.0).

Accepted edge case: if a user-home Codex config switches the native provider away from OpenAI while the OpenClaw route is still `openai`, follow-up turns now run the catalog check too. Ultrafast is still sent only if that catalog lists it for the model.

## Evidence

- **Regression test:** a ChatGPT sign-in thread is resumed, then reused warm, with Ultrafast selected and offered by the catalog. Before the fix: `['priority', 'priority']`. After: `['ultrafast', 'ultrafast']`.
  `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "keeps explicit Ultrafast when a ChatGPT sign-in thread resumes"`
- **Live, OpenClaw 2026.10.1 with this patch applied** (same ChatGPT account and catalog, `gpt-6.1-sol`, Ultrafast selected). Codex app-server log, local time (UTC+2), redacted:

  ```text
  # New thread, then warm turns
  before  19:07:45  turn 1 (thread/start)  ultrafast
          19:07:59  turn 2 (warm)          priority
          19:08:11  turn 3 (warm)          priority
  after   20:16:42  turn 1 (thread/start)  ultrafast
          20:16:47  turn 2 (warm)          ultrafast
          20:16:50  turn 3 (warm)          ultrafast

  # One thread (01a12bf5) started before the patch, resumed after it
  before  19:14:19  turn 1 (thread/start)  ultrafast
          19:14:39  turn 2 (warm)          priority
          19:14:43  turn 3 (warm)          priority
  after   20:30:39  turn 4 (resumed)       ultrafast
          20:30:43  turn 5 (warm)          ultrafast
  ```

  All 10 patched threads on this account (20:16–20:25): 27 of 27 turns `ultrafast`.
- **CI:** all checks on the PR head pass.
- **Local gates:**
  - `pnpm test:extension codex`: 4,931 passed. One failure also fails on clean `main` (`thread-shell-environment.native.test.ts` picks up the host's global git user name).
  - `pnpm check`: changed files clean. The full run reports `max-lines` errors in untouched files, identical on clean `main`. The npm lock guard needs `npm_config_allow_remote=all` under npm 12.2's default config, then passes.
  - `pnpm build`: pass.

<details>
<summary>Technical details</summary>

- Change: `run-attempt-turn-request.ts` passes `modelProvider ?? effectiveRuntimeProviderId` to `resolveCodexUltrafastServiceTier`.
- Why the provider is empty:
  - `normalizeBindingModelProvider` / `resolveCodexAppServerModelProvider` drop `openai` for native ChatGPT auth and user-home connections.
  - Thread start restores the native provider for its own turn (`thread-lifecycle-io.ts`), so turn 1 works.
  - Resume and warm reuse (`thread-lifecycle-warm.ts`) keep the stored empty value. One fix at the consumer covers both.
- Fallback by connection type: supervision connections fall back to `codex` and keep the baseline tier. Explicit custom providers are unchanged.
- Codex applies a per-turn `serviceTier` (`codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs:235`).
- Second ChatGPT account: a resumed turn now sends `model/list` before `turn/start` (before the patch it did not). It stays on Fast; that account's catalog has not offered Ultrafast in these logs.
- `autoreview` (Codex, gpt-6.1-sol, P0–P2): no findings.

</details>

AI-assisted
